transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
To be honest, I'm here because I've been feeling extremely depressed, sad, and completely empty inside for the last 10 months. I just don't have the energy for anything anymore.
Have these symptoms been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the entire 10 months, or have there been clear periods when you felt back to normal?
Yes, it has been like this nearly every single day, most of the day, for the entire 10 months. I haven't had any breaks or periods where I felt back to normal at all.
Before these 10 months, did you experience any long periods of low mood lasting more than two years, or has this been the first time you've felt this way for such a prolonged period?

No, I don't recall ever having a low mood that lasted for over two years before this. This current 10-month period is definitely the first time I've ever experienced such a prolonged period of depression.
During this 10-month period, have you lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities that you used to enjoy?
Yes, definitely. I've completely lost interest in all my usual hobbies and activities over the past 10 months. Even when I try to do them, I don't feel any pleasure or happiness at all.

{
  "category": "symptom presence",
  "subcategory": "appetite",
  "question": "Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight during this time—either an increase or decrease?"
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight. Everything has stayed pretty much the same in that regard.

{
  "category": "symptom presence",
  "subcategory": "sleep",
  "question": "Have you been having trouble with your sleep—such as sleeping too much, too little, or waking up very early and not being able to go back to sleep?"
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns lately. I think I've been sleeping about the same as I usually do, so nothing stands out there.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy almost every day during this period, even when you haven't done much physically?
I haven't particularly noticed feeling unusually tired or lacking physical energy. It is more that I just have absolutely no motivation to start or do anything at all.
Have you been feeling excessive guilt, worthlessness, or self-blame during this time—more than you would expect given your circumstances?
No, I haven't really been experiencing feelings of guilt, worthlessness, or self-blame. I just feel incredibly sad and empty, but I don't feel like I'm to blame for feeling this way.
Have you had trouble concentrating, thinking, or making decisions more than usual during this time?

Yes, my mind has felt incredibly foggy and dazed for the past 10 months, and I find it really hard to focus on simple things like reading or watching TV. Even making minor daily choices, like what to eat or wear, has become exhausting and extremely difficult for me.

Additionally, the patient endorses significant difficulty with concentration and decision-making. Notably, there is no change in appetite, weight, or sleep, and no significant fatigue, guilt, or worthlessness—features that, while common in depression, are not required for diagnosis. The absence of these symptoms does not rule out Major Depressive Disorder, as the core symptoms (depressed mood, anhedonia, cognitive difficulties) are present and causing significant distress. No symptoms suggestive of bipolar disorder, psychosis, anxiety disorders, trauma-related disorders, or eating disorders have emerged. Therefore, Major Depressive Disorder remains the only plausible diagnosis at this time.
